title: High-mass star formation across the Large Magellanic Cloud: I. Chemical properties and hot molecular cores observed with ALMA at 1.2 mm
question: How does sub-solar metallicity in the Large Magellanic Cloud impact high-mass star formation, the formation of different molecular species, and the properties of hot molecular cores?

recipe.goal: Identify compact continuum cores and extract average spectra
recipe.method: Identify 65 compact cores using the 50% peak-intensity contour around intensity peaks (>5 sigma_rms) on 1.2 mm continuum maps (in Paper II), and extract average spectra from primary beam corrected cubes over enclosed pixels.
key_parameters: 50% peak-intensity contour aperture; peak continuum flux > 5 sigma_rms

recipe.goal: Estimate spectral noise and identify molecular transitions
recipe.method: Perform sigma-clipping analysis on each extracted spectrum to determine noise (sigma_rms), classify lines as definite (>5 sigma_rms) or tentative (3-5 sigma_rms), and identify transitions using the CDMS catalog.
key_parameters: Definite detection threshold > 5 sigma_rms; tentative detection threshold 3 to 5 sigma_rms; upper limit threshold S/N < 3

recipe.goal: Model molecular spectra and derive physical parameters (T, N, FWHM, v_LSR)
recipe.method: Solve 1D radiative transfer equation with XCLASS. Fit CH3OH in non-LTE (and LTE for comparison), SO2 and CH3CN in LTE when >2 transitions detected, and fix T for remaining molecules to the CH3OH temperature (or median 27 K). Use a two-layer model (sub-beam hot core + beam-filling cold envelope) for hot cores 4A, 6A, 6B, and 14A.
key_parameters: Beam-filling factor = 1 (for single-component fits and foreground envelope); A/E CH3OH ratio = 1; fixed n_col = 2.0e6 cm^-3 when <=2 CH3OH lines; fixed median T = 27 K when CH3OH undetected; fixed T_e = 10^4 K for H36beta fit
assumptions: All molecular species are located within a core layer at the position of the source (except the 4 two-component hot cores); isotopologues share the same temperature and velocity profile as main species; LAMDA collision rates apply for non-LTE CH3OH.

recipe.goal: Calculate core masses, H2 column densities, and fractional molecular abundances
recipe.method: Calculate dust and gas masses and H2 column densities from 1.2 mm continuum using XCLASS temperatures (in Paper II), then divide molecular column densities N(X) by N(H2) to obtain fractional abundances.
key_parameters: Dust opacity = 1.04 cm^2 g^-1; gas-to-dust mass ratio = 316 (or 320); metallicity scaling factors: 5 (SMC), 2.6 (LMC), 4 (outer Galaxy)
assumptions: 1.2 mm continuum emission originates in optically thin dust; dust and gas are well mixed and have the same temperature.

recipe.goal: Compare observed hot core abundances with chemical models and across galaxies
recipe.method: Compare observed LMC hot core abundances against time-dependent astrochemical models from Acharyya & Herbst (2018) for different initial dust temperatures (10, 15, 20, 25 K), and compare metallicity-scaled abundances across LMC, SMC, and MW hot cores.
key_parameters: Initial dust temperatures = 10, 15, 20, 25 K; final hot core temperatures = 100, 200 K
